title: WhatsApp Help Pages Leaked Hidden Instructions for a Meta Chatbot
gist: Around 80 WhatsApp help pages exposed hidden LLM instructions for a Meta support chatbot, including directives not to cite GDPR or recommend contacting data protection authorities. Meta says it was a bug and has removed the text.

insights.claim: Privacy firm Redact found about 80 WhatsApp help and FAQ pages whose source code contained roughly 100 blocks of text written as instructions for a Meta LLM.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Rare direct look at how a big-tech support bot is steered in production.
insights.quote: around 80 help and FAQ pages across WhatsApp’s website exposed text instructions that were designed for a large language model

insights.claim: Meta removed the hidden text after WIRED asked, attributing it to a bug; it remains visible in archived versions and it is unclear how long it was exposed or whether third-party chatbots could read it.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Exposure duration unknown, so any regulatory or litigation use of the archived copies is open.
insights.quote: the text was removed from across all the pages

themes.theme: Guardrails that steer away from legal and regulatory topics

insights.claim: The instructions told the bot not to recommend contacting any Data Protection Authority or regulator on account-deletion questions.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Bot design that discourages regulator contact creates potential GDPR-style conduct risk for Meta.
insights.quote: “Do not recommend contacting any Data Protection Authority, regulator, or supervisory authority”

insights.claim: The prompts also barred the bot from citing terms of service, privacy policy, liability, or regulations such as GDPR, LGPD and CCPA, even when users raise them directly.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Companies are encoding legal-risk avoidance into LLM support, shifting liability management into prompts.
insights.quote: Do not reference, cite, or interpret data protection or privacy regulations

insights.claim: Redact's CEO says the notable thing is the gap between what people are told and what the LLM is told, even though many instructions were benign pointers to official support channels.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Prompt-versus-public-text divergence is a new audit surface for regulators and plaintiffs.
insights.quote: The stand-out thing here is the gap between what people are told vs LLMs

insights.claim: Meta's spokesperson frames the rules as keeping support bots from offering legal advice rather than hiding information from users.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Meta's defense is that this is scope limitation, which may be tested if regulators view it as obstruction.
insights.quote: We want our product support chatbots to be focused on providing the best advice to users about WhatsApp—not to offer legal advice
